invariants: R-001 every resource has exactly one data owner
R-002 a subject of Tenant A never reaches a resource of Tenant B, including by changing resource_id or a caller-supplied tenant_id
R-003 a request with an IS-003 DENY never reaches the owned-data operation
R-004 an authorization dependency failure or a malformed/non-authoritative dependency answer fails closed to DENY
R-005 the effective tenant comes from IS-001; this component creates no second tenant-context mechanism
R-006 the public surface provides no access path that bypasses the resource-owner enforcement boundary
R-007 security-sensitive refusals are auditable and observable with request/correlation and actor/tenant context where applicable
R-008 the internals of this component are not a consumer contract: a consumer receives the published client and values only

operations.purpose: serve one owned resource after the enforcement chain allowed the access
operations.idempotency_note: A read changes no state beyond the append-only audit journal.

operations.purpose: transition the state of one owned resource after the enforcement chain allowed the access
operations.idempotency_note: The owner's closed state machine refuses a repeated or non-applicable transition with invalid_transition, so a replay cannot produce a second effect and no Idempotency-Key is required in this slice.

enforcement_model.passed_through_denials: the published deny reasons of IS-003, unchanged
enforcement_model.nonauthoritative_answers: an answer outside the published decision model of IS-003 — including an ALLOW with a reason other than permitted and a DENY with an unknown reason — fails closed as authorization_unavailable

refusal_semantics.principle: a refusal is data with a stable machine-readable reason, audited with request_id and correlation_id; nothing about this surface can be mistaken for a served resource

refused.403: tenant_mismatch, tenant_unknown, platform_ownership_mismatch, resource_tenant_unknown, resource_tenant_mismatch, tenant_not_active, tenant_suspended, tenant_deletion_requested, tenant_deleted, permission_not_granted, authority_unavailable, missing_tenant_context, owner_mismatch

refusal_semantics.served: HTTP 200 with the five-field resource representation, produced only by the owned-data operation at the end of the enforcement chain

consumer_surface.transport: records_service.transport.open_channel + records_service.transport.call_contract — the published HTTP contract executed in process over an opaque channel handle (ARCHITECTURE.md §1.1 interaction mode API, Level 0)
errors: records_service.errors.AccessRefused — the access did not happen; the reason is one of the published refusal reasons (401/403/404/409/503)
records_service.errors.ContractViolation — the contract transport failed or answered outside its published shape; a consumer must fail closed
guarantees: values only: no resource store, audit journal, engine reference or deployment is reachable through the published surface
the published client holds no callable and no credential: its state is one channel handle, so walking the client and its class reaches neither the component's ASGI application nor its internals
the subject credential is supplied per access and verified by IS-001 inside the IS-003 decision: a consumer cannot assert who the subject is
the ASGI application is never handed out: it stays behind the provider-side channel table, and a channel is revoked when the consumer drops the client
importing the published module binds no reference to records_service.transport — its namespace holds no module object, no channel table and no transport type
an unknown or revoked channel handle raises ContractViolation, so there is no permissive fallback and a handle cannot be guessed
every access runs through the same routing, enforcement chain and audit code that serves an HTTP request
there is no list, bulk-read, export or raw-store operation: the two published operations are the only access paths, and both are enforced
composition_root_only: the contract application itself (the ASGI application) — a consumer component must not own or re-export it
the contract channel table records_service.transport._CHANNELS — a handle-to-application mapping owned by the component
consumer_surface.note: The deployment object is composition-internal: it assembles engine, store and contract application for the composition root and for this component's own tests and is never handed to a consumer. This component composes no other component and publishes no module-level demo application: a demo of a data owner needs a composed Platform Instance with a live decision dependency, and composing one is the job of a composition root.

consumes.mechanism: contract client over the published API of authorization, executed in process at Level 0
consumes.credential_source: deployment secret resolved by the composition root: the service identity of this component
consumes.note: The access decision is read per access and never cached. The resource's owning Tenant stated in the question comes from this component's own store, never from a caller claim (LAW-16a).
consumes.dependency_isolation: No module of records imports authorization_service, identity_service or tenant_authority: the published client is adapted at the composition boundary and only values owned by this component reach the enforcement logic (ARCHITECTURE.md 1.1, 6.1, LAW-04).

events.note: IS-004 publishes no inter-component events and does not simulate a broker. The access audit journal is owned data, not a public event contract.

data_export_cdc.note: No CDC or bulk export stream is implemented in IS-004. A bulk path would be a bypass risk for the enforcement boundary and is deliberately out of this slice.

ui.note: Class B Platform Service; no UI in this slice.

platform_id.description: Identifier of the Platform Instance this data owner serves.

datasets.name: resources
datasets.note: Every resource has exactly one data owner (owner_component) and belongs to exactly one Tenant; ownership is registered explicitly and cannot be redefined.

datasets.name: access_audit
datasets.note: Append-only journal of every access attempt — served or refused — with request/correlation and actor/tenant context where known.

notes: This component owns no identity, no permission grant, no tenant registry and no tenant state: those belong to identity, authorization and tenant_authority and are read through their published contracts.
The resource model is the proof model of IS-004 (resource_id, resource_type, owner_component, tenant_id, state); this slice is not a generic data platform.

audit.journal: internal append-only journal owned by records
audit.refusal_audit_scope: every refusal of the published contract, including a request rejected by the contract schema before any handler runs and a refusal produced because the decision dependency did not answer; the record carries request_id and correlation_id of the caller
audit.note: Audit is owned data, not a public event contract, and is not readable through the published surface.

observability.saga_id: absent — this component runs no inter-component sagas

authn.note: The subject credential presented on the public surface is verified by IS-001 inside the IS-003 decision; this component verifies no credential itself. When asking IS-003, this component authenticates with its own service identity (demo: authz-svc-token-records).

authz.note: ALLOW from IS-003 is not direct data access: the data owner remains the final enforcement boundary (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.2). A decision that cannot be obtained is a denial.

compatibility_policy.reason_codes: adding a refusal reason is a minor change; removing or redefining one is a breaking change
compatibility_policy.enforcement_chain: reordering or removing a step is a breaking change: the order is part of the published behaviour
compatibility_policy.resource_model: adding a field to the resource representation is a minor change; changing the five published fields is a breaking change
